s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing vascular tumor on the scalp
salient_findings: 8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
Irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa on dermoscopic evaluation
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is 8-mm in size
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation shows irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels
Histopathology shows a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
The structures are covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining shows positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8

shortlist.label: extradigital glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: matches dermoscopic and histopathological findings of a vascular tumor

shortlist.label: proliferating trichilemmal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: slowly growing tumor on the scalp, although less likely given the vascular nature

shortlist.label: cutaneous mastocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: vascular tumor with potential for dermal involvement, but less likely given the specific histopathology

shortlist.label: squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: less likely given the vascular and dermal nature of the tumor, but cannot be entirely ruled out without further information

shortlist.label: pseudolymphomatous folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: less likely, but some dermoscopic features could be considered, although histopathology does not support this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels, intravascular branching papillary structures, and swollen endothelial cells with intracytoplasmic hyaline globules, along with positive CD-31 staining and negative D2-40 and HHV-8 staining, is consistent with an extradigital glomus tumor.

rejected.label: proliferating trichilemmal tumor
rejected.why: The tumor's composition and staining patterns do not match those typical of a proliferating trichilemmal tumor, which is usually associated with hair follicle structures.

rejected.label: cutaneous mastocytoma
rejected.why: The absence of mast cell markers and the presence of vascular structures and hyaline globules do not support a diagnosis of cutaneous mastocytoma.

rejected.label: squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's morphology and immunohistochemical profile do not match those of a squamous cell carcinoma, which typically shows epithelial differentiation and lacks the characteristic vascular features seen in this case.

rejected.label: pseudolymphomatous folliculitis
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features of the tumor do not suggest a pseudolymphomatous folliculitis, which is typically associated with a lymphocytic infiltrate and follicular structures.
